entries.description: Required. FormName must be "ITR-2". AY must be "2025" for FY 2024- 25. Schema version: 1.2. Form version: 1.5.
entries.primarySource: Fixed constants set by the filing software per deployment.
entries.validationSource: Portal validates AY and schema version.
entries.conflictTrigger: Incorrect AY or outdated schema version — portal rejects return.

entries.description: Required. PAN, full name (surname mandatory), date of birth (max 31-Mar- 2025), Aadhaar. Status field distinguishes Individual (I) from HUF (H) — several deductions are blocked for HUF. See inline notes per section.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer profile from e-filing portal onboarding. PAN verified before use.
entries.validationSource: CBDT PAN database for name match Source (Rule 2). UIDAI for Aadhaar-PAN linkage (Rule 3).
entries.conflictTrigger: Name does not match PAN database — Category A (Rule 2). Senior/super- senior citizen status claimed but DOB doesn't match PAN/Aadhaar database — Category A (Rule 3).

entries.description: Required. Enum: RES — Resident NRI — Non- Resident NOR — Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident Determines eligibility for DTAA relief, Schedule FSI, Schedule TR, and several deductions.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declares based on days spent in India during the year and preceding four years.
entries.validationSource: No direct API. Taxpayer declaration. Days-in-India calculation drives the determination.
entries.conflictTrigger: Resident / NOR cannot be classified as FII/FPI — Category A (Rule 20). Non-residents cannot claim Schedule FSI or Schedule TR — Category A (Rules 465, 476). Non-residents cannot claim rebate u/s 87A — Rule 559.

entries.description: Required. Filing section codes: 11 = 139(1) On time 12 = 139(4) Belated 17 = 139(5) Revised 18 = 139(9) Defective response 21 = 139(8A) Updated return Once a proceeding is initiated u/s 148, 153A, or 153C — return cannot be filed u/s 139 (Rule 12).
entries.primarySource: System-determined from current date versus due date. Taxpayer confirms.
entries.validationSource: CBDT portal due date calendar.
entries.conflictTrigger: Old Tax Regime cannot be selected after the section 139(1) due date — Rule 21. Pre-existing notice u/s 148 — Category A (Rule 12). If original return was filed u/s 142(1), revised return is blocked — Rule 4.

entries.description: Required. Y = Old Regime, N = New Regime (default from AY 2024-25). New Regime: blocks most Chapter VI-A deductions, HRA, LTA, professional tax, entertainment allowance. Old Regime: all standard deductions and exemptions apply.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer selects after reviewing tax under both regimes. Product must show comparison.
entries.validationSource: All income and deduction data feeds the comparison calculation.
entries.conflictTrigger: Regime cannot be changed after 139(1) due date — Rule 18. New Regime + prohibited deductions claimed — Category A per individual section.

entries.description: Declarations with follow-on requirements: • Unlisted equity held — details mandatory if 'Yes' (Rule 5) • Director in company — details mandatory if 'Yes' (Rule 10) • FII/FPI — Schedule 115AD proviso requires FiiFpiFlag = Yes (Rule 15) • Portuguese Civil Code (Section 5A) — separate discussion required ★
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declares. Details of directorship / unlisted holdings entered in the respective sub- schedules.
entries.validationSource: No external API. Taxpayer declaration. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Unlisted equity flag = Yes but details blank — Category A (Rule 5). Director flag = Yes but details blank — Category A (Rule 10). FII/FPI = No but 115AD schedule filled — Category A (Rule 15).

entries.description: (per employer block) ITR-2 supports multiple employers in the same year — each is entered as a separate block. Each block captures: 1a: Salary, perquisites, profits in lieu of salary, retirement benefit income (89A), ESOP perquisite 1b: Value of perquisites — detailed breakdown by type 1c: Profits in lieu of salary — by type 1d: Notified country income u/s 89A Same employer cannot claim gratuity or commuted pension more than once — Rules 38, 39.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 (Part A and Part B) from each employer. Annexure 12BA for perquisite details. One Form 16 per employer block.
entries.validationSource: AIS Salary tile. Form 26AS TDS u/s 192. Where two employers exist, product must aggregate both and identify any TDS shortfall.
entries.conflictTrigger: Per employer: Gross Salary must equal sum of 1a+1b+1c+1d+1e+1 f — Rule 22. Total Gross Salary = sum of all employer blocks — Rule 23. Gratuity or commuted pension claimed against more than one employer — Category A (Rules 38, 39). TDS claimed > Income Chargeable under Salary — Category A (Rule 494).

entries.description: Exempt allowances under section 10 — same categories as ITR-1 but across multiple employers. Total exempt u/s 10 (excluding HRA) cannot exceed Gross Salary reduced by HRA — Rule 31. HRA exemption computed via Table 10(13A) and must match the claimed exemption in Schedule S — Rule 722. New Regime: HRA, LTA, 10(14)(i), and 10(14)(ii) allowances blocked — Rule 54.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 Part B — exempt allowances section, per employer. Table 10(13A) requires: city type (metro/non- metro), actual HRA received, actual rent paid, basic salary + DA.
entries.validationSource: AIS salary data. Rules 671–675 govern HRA calculation caps. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime + HRA/LTA/allowanc es claimed — Category A (Rule 54). Same allowance selected more than once — Category A (Rule 51). HRA exemption > actual rent paid − 10% of salary — blocked (Rule 671). 10(10B)(i), (ii), or 10(10C) — only one can be claimed (Rule 47).

entries.description: Standard deduction u/s 16(ia). Old Regime: lower of ₹50,000 or Net Salary — Rule 40. New Regime: lower of ₹75,000 or Net Salary — Rule 655.
entries.primarySource: Auto-applied based on regime. No taxpayer input required.
entries.validationSource: Form 16 Part B— deductions u/s 16.
entries.conflictTrigger: Exceeds applicable cap — Category A.

entries.description: Entertainment allowance u/s 16(ii). Maximum ₹5,000 or 1/5th of basic salary, whichever is lower. Allowed ONLY for Central Government and State Government employees — Rule 35. PSU employees, statutory corporations, and local authorities are NOT eligible for this deduction regardless of how they are classified elsewhere. The Income Tax Act restricts this strictly to Central and State Government employees. New Regime: not allowed — Rule 57.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 Part B.
entries.validationSource: Employer category from PersonalInfo.
entries.conflictTrigger: PSU or any non- Central/State Government employee claims this — Category A (Rule 35). New Regime: any claim — Category A (Rule 57).

entries.description: Professional tax deduction u/s 16(iii). Maximum ₹5,000 — Rule 37. New Regime: not allowed — Rule 58.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 Part B or professional tax payment receipt.
entries.validationSource: No government API. Taxpayer- provided.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: any claim — Category A (Rule 58).

entries.description: Required computed fields: • Net Salary = Total Gross Salary − Exempt allowances u/s 10 − 89A relief (Rule 25) • Deductions u/s 16 = 16(ia) + 16(ii) + 16(iii) (Rule 26) • Income under Head Salaries = Net Salary − Deductions u/s 16 (Rule 27)
entries.primarySource: Computed from upstream fields.
entries.validationSource: Cross- checked against Form 16 Part B totals. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Any computed total does not match formula — Category A (Rules 25–27).

entries.section: 4 Schedule HP — Income from House Prop
entries.description: ITR-2 allows multiple house properties (unlike ITR-1). Each property is entered separately with: • Property type: S=Self-Occupied, L=Let Out, D=Deemed Let Out • Co-ownership flag and taxpayer's percentage share • If co-owned: co- owner PAN and share must total 100% — Rule 68 • Maximum two Self- Occupied properties can claim nil annual value — Rule 80 New Regime: no interest deduction on Self-Occupied properties — Rule 81.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declares each property. Property registration documents for purchase price. Rent agreement / tenancy details for let-out properties.
entries.validationSource: AIS property data. If rent received, cross- checked against AIS rental income and tenant TDS u/s 194IB.
entries.conflictTrigger: Co-owner shares do not total 100% — Category A (Rule 68). Assessee's share is zero but interest on borrowed capital is claimed — Category A (Rule 70). Municipal tax claimed on property with zero rent — Category A (Rule 71). More than two Self- Occupied properties claimed — Category A (Rule 80). New Regime + interest on Self- Occupied — Category A (Rule 81).

entries.section: 4 Schedule HP — Income from House Prop
entries.description: (GrossRent, MunicipalTax, AnnualValue, StdDeduction, InterestBorrowed) Per property computation: • Annual Value = Gross Rent − Municipal Tax (Rule 75) • Standard Deduction = 30% of Annual Value (Rule 67) • Interest on Borrowed Capital via Table 24(b) — bank details and loan details mandatory (Rule 679) • 24(b) row totals must match claimed interest (Rule 677) • 80EE/80EEA interest is claimed over and above 24(b) limit — but loan details in 80EE/80EEA must also appear in 24(b) — Rules 690, 691
entries.primarySource: Home loan interest certificate from bank. Municipal tax receipt. Rent agreement. Table 24(b) — loan- wise breakup.
entries.validationSource: AIS loan interest data. 24(b) totals cross- checked against interest claimed in Schedule HP (Rule 676).
entries.conflictTrigger: Old Regime + Self- Occupied: interest > ₹2,00,000 — Category A (Rule 72). New Regime + Self- Occupied: any interest — Category A (Rule 678). Let Out / Deemed: Gross Rent = zero — Category A (Rule 74). Annual Value ≠ Gross Rent − Municipal Tax — Category A (Rule 75). Standard Deduction ≠ 30% of Annual Value — Category A (Rule 67). 24(b) total ≠ interest claimed in HP — Category A (Rule 676).

entries.description: [Short-Term] — A1: Immovable property — A2: Debt MF/bonds — A4: Listed equity / MF (STT paid) @15% — A5: Other assets @applicable rate — A7: Special rate income — A8: DTAA rates Short-term capital gains arise when the holding period is below the threshold: • Immovable property: < 24 months • Listed equity/MF: < 12 months • Debt MF / bonds: < 36 months For each asset: Full Value of Consideration, Cost of Acquisition, Cost of Improvement, Transfer Expenses, and applicable deductions u/s 54 series are required. If Full Value of Consideration is zero, transfer expenses cannot be claimed — Rules 101–109.
entries.primarySource: Broker P&L statement or Capital Gains Statement (for equity/MF). Sale deed for immovable property. Both acquisition and sale dates must be extracted to confirm STCG classification — holding period check.
entries.validationSource: AIS Capital Gains tile. STT payment records for @15% rate classification.
entries.conflictTrigger: Asset held > 24 months claimed as STCG — Category A (Rule 197). Full Value of Consideration = zero but expenses claimed — Category A (Rules 101–109). Total STCG ≠ sum of individual breakup — Category A (Rule 98).

entries.description: [Long-Term — 23 July 2024 Split] — B1: Land or building — B2: Bonds/debentures — B3: Listed securities — B4: 112A — equity/MF (STT paid) — B5: Shares/debentures of Indian company — B6: Non-resident LTCG — B9: Other assets — B10: Capital Gains Deposit Scheme The critical structural change for AY 2025- 26: ALL LTCG transactions must be split into two buckets based on the date of transfer: • Before 23-Jul- 2024: taxed at 20% with indexation benefit • On or after 23-Jul- 2024: taxed at 12.5% without indexation The product must automatically assign each transaction to the correct bucket based on the extracted sale date. Taxpayer must not be asked to manually select the bucket — this would introduce miscalculation risk. The taxpayer may override the assignment only if they provide a valid reason. For assets acquired before 31-Jan-2018: cost of acquisition is grandfathered to the higher of actual cost or Fair Market Value as on 31-Jan-2018, subject to the cap of the actual sale price (Rule 86, 87).
entries.primarySource: Broker Capital Gains Statement or Capital Gains CSV for equity/MF — sale date and acquisition date must be extracted accurately. Sale deed for immovable property — date of registration is the transfer date. For pre-Jan-2018 acquisitions: BSE/NSE historical price data required to apply grandfathering (FMV as on 31-Jan- 2018).
entries.validationSource: AIS Capital Gains tile. NSE/BSE historical price database for 31-Jan-2018 FMV. Schedule 112A provides line- by-line reconciliation for equity/MF u/s 112A. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Asset held < 24 months claimed as LTCG — Category A (Rule 198). Transfer date = on/after 23-Jul- 2024 but 20% rate applied — Category A (Rule 604). Transfer date = before 23-Jul-2024 but 12.5% rate applied — Category A (Rule 604). Indexation applied on/after 23-Jul- 2024 — blocked (Rule 602). Date of purchase or sale mandatory if LTCG fields are non-zero — Rules 195, 196. Total LTCG ≠ sum of individual breakup — Category A (Rule 99).

entries.description: (LTCG on Listed Equity/MF u/s 112A) Line-by-line detail for every lot of listed equity shares and equity-oriented MF units sold. For each lot: • ISIN, company/fund name • Quantity sold, sale price per unit, total sale value (Col 4 × Col 5) • Acquisition date — determines pre/post 31-Jan-2018 treatment • FMV per unit as on 31-Jan-2018 (applicable only for pre-2018 acquisitions) • Cost of acquisition = higher of actual cost or FMV as on 31-Jan-2018, but capped at sale price • Transfer expenses • Balance (Net LTCG per lot) For acquisitions after 31-Jan-2018 — Columns 4, 5, 10, and 11 must be zero (Rule 186).
entries.primarySource: Broker Capital Gains Statement or Capital Gains CSV. The product must parse this statement and auto-populate each lot. Manual entry for this schedule is not practical for active traders.
entries.validationSource: AIS Capital Gains tile. NSE/BSE historical price data for 31-Jan-2018 FMV. Schedule CG Table B4 must equal total of Column 14 of Schedule 112A — Rule 138.
entries.conflictTrigger: Total Sale Value ≠ Quantity × Price — Category A (Rule 84). Cost of acquisition ≠ higher of Columns 8 and 9 — Category A (Rule 85). FMV Column 9 ≠ lower of Column 6 and Column 11 — Category A (Rule 86). Post-31-Jan-2018 acquisition but FMV/grandfatherin g columns filled — Category A (Rule 186). Schedule 112A total ≠ Schedule CG B4 — Category A (Rule 138).

entries.description: (Virtual Digital Assets — Crypto / NFT) ★ Separate discussion required. All VDA (crypto, NFTs, and other virtual digital assets) transactions are taxed at a flat 30% with no deductions other than cost of acquisition. No set- off against other income is allowed. Each transaction requires: asset type, date of acquisition, date of transfer, consideration received, cost of acquisition, head of income (Capital Gains or Other Sources). The volume of transactions for an active crypto investor makes manual entry impractical. A dedicated tool — similar to KoinX — is required to aggregate transactions from multiple exchanges, compute gains per transaction, and generate a structured import file. This tool must integrate with AIS VDA tile for cross- verification.
entries.primarySource: Crypto exchange transaction history (downloaded CSV from each exchange). A third-party tool is required to consolidate transactions across exchanges, apply FIFO/cost basis methodology, and produce a structured output for the product to import.
entries.validationSource: AIS VDA tile — exchange- reported transaction data. TDS u/s 194S (1% TDS on VDA transfers by specified persons) in Form 26AS. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: VDA income not declared but TDS u/s 194S or 194BA appears in 26AS — Category B (Rule 19). Total VDA income in Schedule VDA ≠ Schedule CG C2 — Category A (Rule 192).

entries.description: (Section 54 series deductions) Capital gains exemptions available: • Section 54: Residential house property sale → reinvestment in residential property • Section 54B: Agricultural land sale → reinvestment in agricultural land • Section 54EC: LTCG → investment in specified bonds (NHAI/REC). Cap: ₹50,00,000 (Rule 650) • Section 54F: Sale of any long-term asset → reinvestment in residential property Deduction in Table D requires detailed breakup. Total deductions per section must match Table D — Rule 177.
entries.primarySource: Investment proof: sale agreement, purchase deed for new property, bond subscription certificate (54EC), bank statements.
entries.validationSource: Sub-registrar property registration data. REC/NHAI bond issuance records.
entries.conflictTrigger: 54EC investment > ₹50,00,000 — Category A (Rule 650). Deductions in Schedule CG Table D ≠ total claimed per section — Category A (Rule 177).

entries.section: 6 Schedule OS — Income from Other Sour
entries.description: (Dividend, Interest, 56(2)(x), Family Pension, 89A income) Gross income at normal applicable rates — broken down by nature: 1a: Dividend income (normal + DTAA) 1b: Interest income (savings, deposits, income tax refund, bonds — each as sub-type) 1c: Rental income from machinery/plant/buil ding 1d: Gifts and other receipts u/s 56(2)(x) 1e: Income from retirement benefit account in notified country u/s 89A Each category must be declared separately. Interest expenditure u/s 57 capped at 20% of dividend income — Rule 229.
entries.primarySource: AIS pre-filled data for dividend and interest. Bank interest certificates for FD interest. Rental agreement for machinery/building rentals.
entries.validationSource: AIS dividend tile (SFT from registrar/trans fer agents). Form 26Q (TDS on interest). Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Deduction u/s 57 claimed but no income under the corresponding head — Category A (Rule 241). Depreciation on machinery rental only allowed if rental income is non-zero — Category A (Rule 205). Interest expenditure on dividends > 20% of dividend income — Category A (Rule 229).

entries.section: 6 Schedule OS — Income from Other Sour
entries.description: (115BB) IncFrmOnGames (115BBJ) Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, horse races — taxed at 30% u/s 115BB. Winnings from online games — taxed u/s 115BBJ. Both taxed at flat rates with no deductions. Anonymous donations u/s 115BBC are not applicable in ITR-2 — Rule 246.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declaration. Winning slips or operator-issued certificates.
entries.validationSource: AIS winnings data. TDS u/s 194B (lottery) and 194BA (online games) in Form 26AS.
entries.conflictTrigger: Lottery/online game winnings declared but not offered in Schedule SI at the corresponding special rate — Category A (Rules 388, 440). Anonymous donation u/s 115BBC claimed — Category A (Rule 246).

entries.section: 6 Schedule OS — Income from Other Sour
entries.description: — Deductions u/s 57 (Family Pension, Interest costs) Allowed deductions: • Family pension (FAP): lower of ₹15,000 or 1/3rd of pension — Old Regime (Rule 228). Up to ₹25,000 under New Regime. • Interest expense on dividend u/s 57(1): capped at 20% of gross dividend — Rule 229. • Other deductions u/s 57: only allowed if corresponding income is declared in Sl.No. 1b, 1c, 1d, or 1e — Rule 230.
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declaration for family pension. Interest expense records for dividend- related borrowings.
entries.validationSource: AIS pension and dividend data.
entries.conflictTrigger: Family pension deduction claimed but family pension income not declared — Category A (Rule 222). Deduction u/s 57 claimed with no corresponding income — Category A (Rule 230).

entries.section: §7 Schedule CYLA — Current Year Loss S
entries.description: (House Property Loss, Capital Loss, Other Source Loss) Sets off current year losses against current year income. Key rules: • House property loss cap: ₹2,00,000 under Old Regime — Rule 265 • New Regime: house property loss cannot be set off against any other income — Rule 283. The loss cannot be carried forward either — Rule 284. • OS normal loss must be set off against race horse income first — Rule 286. • Total loss set off cannot exceed the income available — Rule 285. CYLA income feeds BFLA. CYLA figures must match Schedule CG Table E — Rules 273–282.
entries.primarySource: Computed from Schedule HP, Schedule CG Table E, and Schedule OS. Pre-filled from current year schedules.
entries.validationSource: All constituent schedules cross- checked. Schedule CG Table E provides capital loss set-off workings.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: HP loss set off against any income — Category A (Rule 283). Old Regime: HP loss set off > ₹2,00,000 — Category A (Rule 265). CYLA figures don't match source schedules — Category A (Rules 266, 267, 281). Loss set off > income available — Category A (Rule 287).

entries.description: (BF House Property, BF Capital Losses, BF Speculation Loss) Sets off brought- forward losses from prior years against the current year's income remaining after CYLA. Loss types and carry-forward periods: • House property loss: 8 years • Short-term capital loss: 8 years (can set off against STCG and LTCG) • Long-term capital loss: 8 years (can set off against LTCG only) • Speculation loss: 4 years (against speculation profit only) BFLA Sl.no. 1 figures must match CYLA Sl.no. 4 for each income type — Rules 252–262. BF loss utilised in BFLA must not exceed the balance in CFL Column 3 — Rule 288.
entries.primarySource: Auto-fetched from the Income Tax portal's pre-fill data based on the previous year's ITR acknowledgement. Taxpayer may override if a rectification order or revised return has updated the brought- forward position that the portal's pre-fill does not yet reflect.
entries.validationSource: Schedule CFL — the prior year's carried- forward loss schedule. Portal pre-fill data. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: BFLA Sl.no. 1 figures don't match CYLA Sl.no. 4 — Category A (Rules 252–262). BF loss utilised > loss available in CFL — Category A (Rule 288). CFL adjustment amount ≠ BFLA adjustment — Category A (Rules 264, 295).

entries.description: (AY2017-18 through AY2024-25 + Current Year AY2025-26) Carries forward all current and prior year unabsorbed losses for up to 8 assessment years. Each AY row carries: HP loss, STCL (@15%, @20%, @30%, applicable rate, DTAA), LTCL (@10%, @12.5%, @20%, DTAA), OS normal loss, racehorse loss. STCL and LTCL from Schedule CG Table E must feed CFL — Rules 291, 292. HP loss from CYLA feeds CFL — Rule 293. Total brought- forward losses must match sum of individual AY rows — Rule 294.
entries.primarySource: Current year losses: auto-computed from CYLA and Schedule CG Table E. Prior year losses: auto-fetched from portal pre-fill. Override allowed with valid reason (e.g., rectification order or revised return).
entries.validationSource: Portal pre-fill data. Schedule CG Table E for STCL/LTCL. CYLA for HP and OS losses.
entries.conflictTrigger: STCL in CFL ≠ Table E STCL remaining after set- off — Category A (Rule 291). LTCL in CFL ≠ Table E LTCL remaining after set- off — Category A (Rule 292). HP loss in CFL ≠ CYLA HP loss remaining — Category A (Rule 293). Total BF losses ≠ sum of individual AY rows — Category A (Rule 294).

entries.description: 80CCC 80CCDEmployeeOrSE (combined cap ₹1,50,000) Combined ceiling for 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) = ₹1,50,000 — Old Regime only. New Regime: all three must be zero — Rule 361. HUF: 80CCD(1), 80CCC are not allowed — Rules 336. PRAN must be provided for 80CCD(1) — Rule 714. Schedule 80C — each investment requires amount and document identification number — Rule 711. 80C total must match Schedule 80C — Rule 712.
entries.primarySource: LIC receipts, EPF/PPF statements, ELSS statements, school fee receipts, loan principal repayment certificate.
entries.validationSource: AIS insurance, EPF, PPF data. Schedule 80C item totals cross- checked. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Combined 80C+80CCC+80CC D(1) > ₹1,50,000 — Category A (Rule 365). New Regime: any claim — Category A (Rule 361). HUF claims 80CCD(1) — Category A (Rule 336). PRAN not provided — blocked (Rule 714).

entries.description: Additional NPS contribution by employee or self- employed — separate from the ₹1,50,000 limit. Cap: ₹50,000 Old Regime. New Regime: not allowed. HUF: not allowed — Rule 337. PRAN mandatory — Rule 714.
entries.primarySource: NPS account statement.
entries.validationSource: NPS Trust / NSDL CRA.
entries.conflictTrigger: HUF claims 80CCD(1B) — Category A (Rule 337). New Regime: any claim — Category A (Rule 361).

entries.description: Employer NPS contribution. Caps: • Central / State Govt employer: 14% of salary — Rule 358 • Other employers (Old Regime): 10% of salary — Rule 364 • New Regime (all employers): 14% of salary — Rule 657 Pensioner employer categories (CG, SG, PSU, Others): this deduction is blocked — Rule 357. HUF: not allowed — Rule 338.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 Part B — employer NPS contribution row.
entries.validationSource: AIS NPS Employer Contribution data.
entries.conflictTrigger: Pensioner employer category + 80CCD(2) claimed — Category A (Rule 357). Exceeds applicable percentage — Category A. HUF claims 80CCD(2) — Category A (Rule 338).

entries.description: Agniveer Corpus Fund contribution. Capped at 60% of salary — Rule 366. Available only to Central Government employees enrolled in the Agnipath scheme. Not allowed in New Regime — Rule 369.
entries.primarySource: Payroll certificate from Central Government / Ministry of Defence for Agniveer enrolees. Treated as a manual declaration — applicable to a small subset of filers.
entries.validationSource: Ministry of Defence payroll.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime — blocked (Rule 369). Amount > 60% of salary — Category A (Rule 366).

entries.description: Health insurance premium deduction. Old Regime only. New Regime: blocked — Rule 323. HUF: Sl.no.2 (parents) not applicable — Rule 651. Same caps as ITR- 1: Self/Family ₹25,000 or ₹50,000 (senior citizen), Parents ₹25,000 or ₹50,000 (senior citizen), combined max ₹1,00,000. Insurer name and policy number mandatory per insured row — Rules 680–683. Schedule 80D must be filled if 80D is claimed in VIA — Rule 321. 80D in VIA must equal eligible amount in Schedule 80D — Rule 322.
entries.primarySource: Health insurance premium receipts. Schedule 80D with insurer-wise breakup.
entries.validationSource: AIS insurance premium data. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: any claim — Category A (Rule 323). HUF: parents deduction — blocked (Rule 651). Schedule 80D not filled — blocked (Rule 321).

entries.description: 80U 80DD: Dependent disability. 80U: Self- disability. Old Regime only. Not available to Non-Residents — Rules 346, 348. HUF: 80U not allowed. 80DD: allowed for 'Member of HUF' only — Rule 574. Form 10IA (for autism/cerebral palsy/multiple disabilities) must be filed separately — Rule 688. If deduction > 0, supporting details mandatory — Rules 382, 384.
entries.primarySource: Schedule 80U or 80DD: nature of disability, certificate, UDID number, Form 10IA if applicable.
entries.validationSource: UDID database where applicable.
entries.conflictTrigger: Non-Resident claims 80DD or 80U — Category A (Rules 346, 348). New Regime: any claim — blocked (Rule 361). Details not provided when deduction > 0 — blocked.

entries.description: Treatment of specified diseases. Old Regime only. New Regime: blocked. Non-Resident: not allowed — Rule 347. Details of specified disease mandatory — Rule 716.
entries.primarySource: Medical certificate from specialist. Disease from CBDT- notified list.
entries.validationSource: No government API. Taxpayer- provided.
entries.conflictTrigger: Non-Resident claims 80DDB — Category A (Rule 347). New Regime: any claim — blocked.

entries.description: 80EE 80EEA 80EEB Education and housing loan deductions — same rules as ITR-1 (loan dates, stamp value caps, mutual exclusion of 80EE and 80EEA). HUF: None of these deductions are allowed — Rules 339, 340, 344, 345. For 80EE and 80EEA: loan details in the respective schedules must also appear in Table 24(b) of Schedule HP — Rules 690, 691. 80EE / 80EEA can only be claimed once the 24(b) limit is exhausted — Rule 689.
entries.primarySource: Loan sanction certificate, interest certificate from bank. Schedule 80E/80EE/80EEA/80 EEB with loan-wise details.
entries.validationSource: AIS loan data. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: HUF claims any of 80E, 80EE, 80EEA, 80EEB — Category A (Rules 339, 340, 344, 345). New Regime: any claim — blocked (Rule 361). 80EE + 80EEA both non-zero — Category A.

entries.description: (Schedule 80G) Donations to approved funds and charities. Old Regime only. New Regime: Schedule 80G must be blank — Rule 308. Donee PAN must not match assessee PAN or verification PAN — Rule 296. Same Donee PAN cannot appear in more than one block (100%/50%/with limit/without limit) — Rule 309. Cash donations above ₹2,000 disallowed across all tables — Rules 298– 301. Schedule 80G deduction ≤ eligible amount — Rule 297. Exception: PAN 'AAAAR1077P' (PM Relief Fund) may appear in multiple blocks — Rule 309.
entries.primarySource: Schedule 80G: donation receipts with Donee name, PAN, ARN, amount in cash vs other mode.
entries.validationSource: Donee PAN verification. NGO/Trust registration database.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: any claim — Category A. Cash donation > ₹2,000 — disallowed. Donee PAN = Assessee PAN — Category A (Rule 296). Same Donee PAN across multiple blocks — Category A (Rule 309).

entries.description: (Schedule 80GGA) Donations to scientific research or rural development. Old Regime only. New Regime: blocked — Rule 334. Cash > ₹2,000 not allowed — Rule 335. Donee PAN must not match assessee PAN — Rule 332. Schedule 80GGA mandatory if 80GGA claimed — Rule 333.
entries.primarySource: Donation receipts with Donee PAN, cash/other mode split.
entries.validationSource: Donee PAN verification. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: blocked. Schedule not filled when deduction claimed — blocked (Rule 333).

entries.description: (Schedule 80GGC) Political party contributions. Only non-cash contributions eligible. Contribution date must be within AY 2024-25 (01-Apr- 2024 to 31-Mar- 2025) — Rule 573. Eligible amount per row = contribution in other mode, capped at GTI — Rule 371. Date of contribution mandatory if amount > 0 — Rule 375.
entries.primarySource: Contribution receipts. Date and mode of payment required.
entries.validationSource: Electoral trust records.
entries.conflictTrigger: Cash contribution — not eligible. Contribution date outside AY — blocked. Details missing — blocked (Rules 375, 376).

entries.description: 80RRB 80QQB: Royalty from books authored by an Individual (not HUF) resident in India. Max ₹3,00,000. 80RRB: Royalty from patents registered on or after 01-Apr-2003. Max ₹3,00,000. Both deductions: not available to Non- Residents or HUF — Rules 352–355. Critical rule: these deductions are automatically disallowed if the return is filed after the section 139(1) due date — Rules 359, 360. The product must check the filing date and zero out these deductions if the return is belated. Form 10CCD acknowledgement required for 80QQB — Rule 717. Form 10CCE acknowledgement required for 80RRB — Rule 718.
entries.primarySource: Royalty agreement. Book publisher's certificate or patent certificate. Form 10CCD / Form 10CCE acknowledgement from portal.
entries.validationSource: CBDT patent registry (for 80RRB). Filed Form 10CCD/10CC E on portal.
entries.conflictTrigger: Return filed after 139(1) due date — both deductions are automatically blocked and set to zero. Non-Resident or HUF claims either deduction — Category A. Form acknowledgement not provided — blocked.

entries.description: 80TTB 80TTA: Savings account interest, max ₹10,000. Old Regime. Not for Senior Citizens — Rule 341. Restricted to savings account interest only — Rule 362. New Regime: blocked. 80TTB: Senior Citizen interest (savings + deposits), max ₹50,000. Old Regime. Not for non- residents — Rule 368. Restricted to interest income from other sources — Rule 363. New Regime: blocked. HUF: neither applies.
entries.primarySource: AIS Interest tile.
entries.validationSource: AIS savings and deposit interest data. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Senior Citizen claims 80TTA — Category A (Rule 341). Non-Senior claims 80TTB — blocked. Non-Resident claims 80TTB — Category A (Rule 368). New Regime: any claim — blocked.

entries.description: Rent paid deduction where no HRA received. Max: least of ₹60,000/year, 25% of total income, or rent paid minus 10% of income. Form 10BA must be filed — Rule 715 (Category D). Cannot be claimed alongside HRA exemption u/s 10(13A) — Rule 52. Note: If HRA is claimed, 80GG is capped at ₹55,000 — Rule 52.
entries.primarySource: Form 10BA acknowledgement. Monthly rent and landlord details.
entries.validationSource: AIS.
entries.conflictTrigger: HRA exemption and 80GG both claimed simultaneously — Category A (Rule 52). Form 10BA not filed — Category D warning.

entries.description: Alternate Minimum Tax applies where adjusted total income exceeds ₹20,00,000. Rate: 18.5% of adjusted total income — Rule 450. Old Regime only. New Regime: Schedule AMT must be blank — Rule 452. Adjusted Total Income = Total Income (Part B-TI) + deductions claimed u/s 80QQB and 80RRB — Rule 443. If AMT tax > normal tax: Form 29C is mandatory — Category D Rule 1.
entries.primarySource: Computed from Part B-TI and Schedule VIA figures.
entries.validationSource: Cross- checked against Part B-TI — Rule 441.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: Schedule AMT filled — Category A (Rule 452). AMT tax > normal tax but Form 29C not filed — Category D. Adjusted Total Income ≠ Part B-TI + VIA deductions — Category A (Rule 442).

entries.description: (AMT Credit Carry Forward & Utilisation) Tracks AMT credit accumulated in prior years and utilised in the current year. Credit available = AMT paid − Normal Tax in prior years. Credit cannot exceed AMT − Normal Tax for the current year — Rule 447. Prior year AMT credit: auto-fetched from portal pre-fill. New Regime: Schedule AMTC columns C and D must be zero — Rule 453.
entries.primarySource: Prior year AMTC data from portal pre-fill. Current year AMT computation from Schedule AMT.
entries.validationSource: Portal pre-fill for carried- Source forward AMT credit.
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: AMTC columns C/D non-zero — Category A (Rule 453). Credit utilised > available — Category A (Rule 447).

entries.section: 12 Schedule SI — Income Taxable at Spe
entries.description: Consolidates all income taxable at special rates — must match the respective source schedules: • 115BB: Lottery / gambling winnings — 30% • 115BBJ: Online game winnings — 30% • 111A / 115AD proviso: STCG on equity (STT paid) — 15% (before 23-Jul- 2024) / 20% (on/after) • 112A / 115AD proviso: LTCG on equity — 10% or 12.5% • 112: LTCG on other assets — 20% • DTAA special rates: as per applicable treaty Schedule SI tax (column ii) = taxable income × applicable rate — Rule 391.
entries.primarySource: Fed from Schedule CG (capital gains at special rates), Schedule OS (lottery, online games, dividends at special rates), Schedule BFLA (brought- forward losses set-off against special rate income).
entries.validationSource: All constituent schedules cross- checked. Schedule BFLA Sl.no. 3 must match Schedule SI — Rule 390.
entries.conflictTrigger: Special income in Schedule SI not offered in the source schedule (CG/OS/BFLA) — Category A (Rules 385–440). Tax computed ≠ income × special rate — Category A (Rule 391). Schedule SI tax total ≠ sum of individual rows — Category A (Rule 399). Special income declared in Part B- TI but not in respective schedules — Category A (Rule 539).

entries.description: (Agricultural, PF receipts, Exempt DTAA income, Pass-through income) Exempt income that is not included in total income: • Net Agricultural Income = Gross receipts − Agriculture expenditure − Unabsorbed agricultural loss of prior 8 years (Rule 458) • If net agricultural income > ₹5,00,000: details of each agricultural land must be provided — Rule 468 • Other exempt income: PF receipts, insurance policy receipts, scholarships, etc. • DTAA-exempt income: income not chargeable as per treaty • Pass-through income: from Schedule PTI • New Regime: 10(17) allowance for MP/MLA/MLC not allowed — Rule 467
entries.primarySource: Taxpayer declaration. Land records for agricultural income. DTAA treaty reference for exempt DTAA income.
entries.validationSource: AIS Exempt Income tile. Schedule PTI for pass- through. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: New Regime: 10(17) MLA/MLC allowance claimed — Category A (Rule 467). Agricultural income > ₹5,00,000 but land details not filled — Category A (Rule 468). Exempt DTAA income total ≠ sum of individual entries — Category A (Rule 456).

entries.description: / IncFromHP / IncCapGain / IncOthSrc ★ Separate discussion required. Schedule FSI is applicable only to Resident and NOR individuals. Non- Residents cannot file Schedule FSI — Rule 465. For each foreign country: • Country name and code • Taxpayer Identification Number in that country • Income by head: Salary, House Property, Capital Gains, Other Sources • Tax paid in that country (column c) • Tax deductible in India (column d) = tax computed on that income per Indian rates • Relief available (column e) = lower of (c) or (d) Total of FSI column b (foreign income included in Part B- TI) must reconcile with salary/HP/CG/OS amounts declared — Rules 466, 469–471.
entries.primarySource: Foreign salary slip or employer certificate for salary income abroad. Foreign bank statements, property documents, or broker statements for other heads. Tax assessment order or tax payment receipt from the foreign country for taxes paid.
entries.validationSource: No direct API for foreign income/taxes. Taxpayer- provided documents only. Cross- checked against Part B-TI income by head. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Non-Resident files Schedule FSI — Category A (Rule 465). FSI salary income > Schedule S gross salary — Category A (Rule 469). FSI HP income > Schedule HP — Category A (Rule 470). FSI capital gains > Schedule CG — Category A (Rule 471).

entries.description: ★ Separate discussion required. Tax relief on foreign income — applicable to Residents only. Non-Residents cannot file Schedule TR — Rule 476. Two types of relief: • Section 90 / 90A (DTAA countries): relief limited to the lower of foreign tax paid or Indian tax on that income. Form 67 is mandatory if relief u/s 90/91 is claimed — Category D Rule 3. • Section 91 (non- DTAA countries): unilateral relief. For resident taxpayers, DTAA benefit on rate of taxation is not available. DTAA relief is available under Schedule TR and FSI only — Category D Rule 13. Total taxes paid outside India = sum of column c in Schedule FSI per country — Rule 477. Total relief = sum of column e in Schedule FSI per country — Rule 478.
entries.primarySource: Form 67 filed on portal. Foreign tax payment receipts. Schedule FSI tax relief amounts feed into Schedule TR.
entries.validationSource: Schedule FSI cross- checked against Schedule TR totals — Rules 477, 478.
entries.conflictTrigger: Non-Resident files Schedule TR — Category A (Rule 476). Relief > lower of foreign tax or Indian tax — blocked. Form 67 not filed — Category D (Rule 3). Resident claims DTAA rate benefit directly in Schedule OS — Category D warning (Rule 13).

entries.description: (Foreign Bank Accounts, Foreign Equity/Debt, Foreign Immovable Property, Other Foreign Assets, Foreign Trusts, Other Foreign Income Sources) Mandatory for Resident individuals with any foreign assets or signing authority over foreign accounts. Covers: Foreign bank accounts, custodial accounts, equity and debt interests, cash value insurance, immovable property abroad, financial interests in foreign entities, other foreign assets, trust interests outside India. Non-Residents are exempt from Schedule FA. Failure to disclose foreign assets has Black Money Act consequences — not just income tax penalties.
entries.primarySource: Foreign bank statements. Foreign broker statements. Foreign property documents. Entity ownership certificates.
entries.validationSource: No government API. Taxpayer- provided documents only. High risk of non- disclosure — product must prompt explicitly. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Resident with foreign assets who leaves Schedule FA blank — compliance risk. Product must ask 'Do you hold any foreign assets or foreign bank accounts?' as a mandatory pre- check.

entries.description: (Bank deposits, Shares, Insurance, Cash, Jewellery, Vehicles) Mandatory only if total income exceeds ₹50 lakhs Immovable assets: address, ownership details, and cost of acquisition for each property. Movable assets: • Bank deposits — auto-populated from bank details section • Shares and securities — auto- populated from Schedule CG / broker data where available • Insurance policies — taxpayer declares cost of premiums • Cash in hand — taxpayer declares • Jewellery, bullion, artwork — taxpayer declares • Vehicles, yachts, aircraft — taxpayer declares Liabilities related to assets: total outstanding loans against the above assets.
entries.primarySource: Self-declaration. Product auto- populates bank balances from bank account details and asset values from Schedule CG / Schedule HP where already captured. For remaining items (jewellery, cash, vehicles), simplified declaration UI.
entries.validationSource: AIS does not directly cross- check Schedule AL, but a significant discrepancy between declared assets and AIS-reported transactions is a scrutiny trigger.
entries.conflictTrigger: Total income > ₹50 lakhs but Schedule AL not filled — submission blocked (Rule 479). Glaring discrepancy between declared assets and AIS- reported values — product should flag for taxpayer review before submission.

entries.description: ★ Separate discussion required. Applicable only to taxpayers in Goa, Daman & Diu governed by the Portuguese Civil Code, where income from HP, Capital Gains, and Other Sources is split 50/50 between spouses. Spouse PAN is mandatory if Section 5A is selected — Rule 472. If Section 5A is selected as 'Yes': Schedule 5A must be filled and filed. If selected as 'No': Schedule 5A must be blank — Rules 6, 14.
entries.primarySource: Joint declaration by both spouses. Income details from HP, CG, and OS schedules are apportioned 50/50.
entries.validationSource: Spouse PAN verified against PAN database. Schedule 5A totals cross- Source checked against Schedule HP, CG, OS.
entries.conflictTrigger: Section 5A = Yes but Schedule 5A not filled — Category A (Rule 6). Section 5A = No but Schedule 5A is filled — Category A (Rule 14). Spouse PAN and assessee PAN are the same — Category A (Rule 82 for co-owned property).

entries.section: 18 Schedule ESOP — Deferred Tax on Sta
entries.description: Available to employees of DPIIT- registered eligible startups u/s 80-IAC who have received ESOPs as a perquisite u/s 17(2)(vi). Tax on ESOP perquisites is deferred until the earlier of: • Sale of the shares • End of 5 years from the year of allotment • Date of cessation of employment Required fields per year: • Tax attributed to ESOP perquisite • Tax deferred brought forward from prior year • Tax payable in current year (triggered by any of the three events above) • Balance deferred to be carried forward HUF cannot file Schedule ESOP — Rule 572. Balance deferred (Sl.no 8) = Sl.no 3 − 7. This balance must also match Sl.no 3b of Part B-TTI — Rules 503, 504.
entries.primarySource: Form 16 from the startup employer and Annexure 12BA — which specifically reports ESOP perquisite value and any tax deferred. DPIIT registration number from the employer's certificate.
entries.validationSource: DPIIT- registered startup database. Form 16 ESOP perquisite amount cross- checked against Schedule ESOP. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: HUF files Schedule ESOP — Category A (Rule 572). Balance deferred ≠ Sl.no 3 − 7 — Category A (Rule 503). Balance deferred ≠ Part B-TTI Sl.no 3b — Category A (Rule 504). Sl.no 5 = Yes (shares sold): deferred tax must be recognised in current year — Rule 506.

entries.section: 19 Part B-TI & Part B-TTI — Total Income
entries.description: (STCG+LTCG) Aggregates all income heads and losses: • Salaries = Schedule S final figure (Rule 517) • HP = Schedule HP final figure (Rule 518) • Capital Gains = STCG + LTCG + VDA (Rules 519– 525) • OS = Schedule OS final figure (Rule 526) • GTI = sum of above after CYLA and BFLA (Rule 531) • Total Income = GTI − Chapter VI-A deductions (Rule 532) Net agricultural income feeds rate calculation — Rule 534. Deemed income u/s 115JC from Schedule AMT — Rule 537.
entries.primarySource: Computed from all constituent schedules.
entries.validationSource: All schedule figures cross- checked at aggregation. Rule 531 is the primary GTI reconciliation check.
entries.conflictTrigger: GTI ≠ sum of individual head incomes — Category A (Rule 531). Total Income ≠ GTI − VIA deductions — Category A (Rule 532). Schedule not filled for a head claimed in Part B-TI — Category A (Rules 517–528). GTI is nil but tax computation is disclosed — Category A (Rule 510).

entries.section: 19 Part B-TI & Part B-TTI — Total Income
entries.description: Final tax computation: • Tax on Total Income per slab (normal) + special rate tax from Schedule SI • Surcharge: 10% (income 50L–1Cr), 15% (1Cr–2Cr), 25% (2Cr–5Cr), 37% (above 5Cr). Separate surcharge for 115BBE income at 25%. • Education Cess: 4% • Rebate u/s 87A: Old Regime — max ₹12,500 if TI ≤ ₹5,00,000 (Rule 508). New Regime — max ₹25,000. Not available to NRI or HUF — Rules 559, 560. • AMT credit u/s 115JD from Schedule AMTC • Relief u/s 89, 90/90A, 91 from Schedule TR • Interest u/s 234A, 234B, 234C, 234F
entries.primarySource: Computed from Part B-TI and all constituent schedules.
entries.validationSource: Cross- checked against all source schedules. Part B-TTI is the final reconciliation point. Source
entries.conflictTrigger: Rebate > ₹12,500 in Old Regime — Category A (Rule 508). Rebate claimed by NRI or HUF — Category A (Rules 559, 560). Total Income > marginal relief break-even point (approx. ₹7,27,770) in New Regime but rebate claimed — Category A (Rule 507). Gross tax payable < higher of normal tax or AMT — Category A (Rule 565). Tax paid in schedules ≠ Part B- TTI tax paid — Category A (Rule 516).

entries.section: 19 Part B-TI & Part B-TTI — Total Income
entries.description: (TDS, TCS, Advance Tax, Self-Assessment Tax) Same structure as ITR-1: TDS from Schedules TDS1/TDS2/TDS3, TCS from Schedule TCS, advance tax and SAT from Schedule IT. BFSI: IFSC must match RBI database — Rule 558. Refund = Total Taxes Paid − Total Tax and Interest payable — Rule 562. Tax payable = Total Tax and Interest − Total Taxes Paid — Rule 563. Part B-TTI TCS Sl.no 15c must match Schedule TCS total — Rule 483.
entries.primarySource: Form 26AS / AIS for TDS and TCS. OLTAS for advance tax and SAT challans.
entries.validationSource: TRACES 26AS. OLTAS database.
entries.conflictTrigger: TCS claimed > TCS collected — Category A (Rule 481). TDS claimed > TDS deducted — Category A (Rule 489). Advance tax total ≠ Schedule IT entries in advance tax date range — Category A (Rule 547). IFSC not in RBI database — Category A (Rule 558).

entries.description: (Income from AIF/Business Trust) Pass-through income from Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) or Business Trusts (REITs/InvITs) that passes through to the investor without being taxed at the fund level. Breakup required: STCG, LTCG, Other Sources, Exempt income. Schedule PTI feeds Schedule HP (pass- through HP income), Schedule OS, Schedule EI, and Schedule CG. Schedule PTI Col 9 = Col 7 − Col 8 — Rule 459.
entries.primarySource: Annual investor statement from AIF or Business Trust manager — issued to unit holders after year end.
entries.validationSource: Cross- checked against Schedule HP, CG, OS, and EI for consistency.
entries.conflictTrigger: Pass-through HP income in Schedule PTI ≠ Schedule HP pass- through field — Category A (Rule 79). Pass-through exempt income in Schedule EI ≠ Schedule PTI — Category A (Rule 454). PTI Col 9 ≠ Col 7 − Col 8 — Category A (Rule 459).
